source.note: The source is this repository's own Python implementation, not a second checkout. Cadenza is being rewritten in place (cadenza#8): `src/cadenza/` and `tests/` are the specification until a later PR retires them, so every inventory here is collected from the working tree at the recorded revision.

suite_baseline.reconciliation: `PYTHONPATH=src PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider` at a5672f8 on CPython 3.12.3: 330 passed. No module is skipped at collection time, so collected == the sum of the eight per-file inventories with nothing left over. See parity/source-inventory.manifest.json.

file.note: 39 test functions, 50 collected node ids: four functions are parametrized (schema versions over 4, wrongly shaped tables over 5, missing required fields over 3, non-boolean tombstones over 3). The ledger counts node ids, for the reason recorded in DECISIONS.md D-0010.

systematic_mappings.to: a `refusal(Kind, () => ...)` helper in `test/support.ts` that returns the error, then `caught.message` and `caught.location`
systematic_mappings.why: `expect(...).toThrow(Kind)` checks the class and `toThrow(/re/)` checks the message, but neither yields the INSTANCE, and 14 of these cases go on to assert `location`. The helper is `pytest.raises(...) as caught`, with the same failure when nothing is raised. It also fixes what `match=` means: pytest matches `str(exc)`, which includes the location, so `CatalogError.message` in the port carries the FORMATTED text and the bare text moves to `.detail`. Spelled the other way round, every translated `match=` would silently stop seeing the location.
systematic_mappings.affects: every case that asserts a refusal (30 of the 50)

systematic_mappings.to: `makeLayer(data, options)` / `gitUrlProject(options)` from `test/support.ts`, with an explicit `extra` object
systematic_mappings.why: TypeScript has no `**kwargs`. The one property that had to be preserved is ORDER: `table.update(extra)` appends the extras AFTER `source` and `base_branch`, and `refuseUnknownKeys` reports the first offending key it meets, so moving the extras to the front would change which key a refusal names.

A frozen plain object is the faithful `MappingProxyType`: a property assignment on one throws `TypeError` in strict mode, which is what the source's last case observes. A `Map` would have kept only the compile-time claim. The object is safe from JavaScript's integer-like key reordering because every key is a `project_id`, an alias or a fixed field name, and `^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$` cannot spell an array index.
systematic_mappings.affects: the cases that compare a whole mapping (4)

systematic_mappings.why: Python's `in` on a dict tests its own keys. JavaScript's `in` also finds inherited ones, and a plain object inherits from `Object.prototype`, so a name such as `constructor` would answer the wrong way. `Object.hasOwn` is the question the source asks.

systematic_mappings.to: `baseDir: CATALOG_DIR` (an absolute path built for this platform)
systematic_mappings.why: The three `allowed_local_roots` cases take `tmp_path` only because they need SOME absolute directory; none of them touches a filesystem. `test/support.ts` provides one that is absolute on Windows as well -- where a drive-less path is drive-relative and `layerDocument` refuses it -- which is why the source's own `tests/support.py` builds paths the same way.

ids: test/application/compose.test.ts::section 5.2: schema version > a number with a fractional part is refused
target_only_tests.why: One test, standing where `test_non_integer_schema_version_is_refused[1.0]` could not be translated. That source case refuses a Python FLOAT whose value is 1, and JavaScript has a single numeric type in which `1.0 === 1`, so no value reproduces it. The branch is real and would otherwise be untested, so the nearest property that DOES exist -- a number with a fractional part is refused -- is asserted instead. It is declared here rather than mapped, because it is not that source case: it is what is left of it.

inherited_limitations.behaviour: `composeCatalog` calls `parseCloneSource`, `parseIdentifier` and `parseBaseBranch`, and this belt ports NONE of their test files: `tests/test_clone_source.py` (57 cases), `tests/test_identifiers.py` (25) and `tests/test_refs.py` (62) stay `inventoried`. The three functions are implemented here because a composer that cannot read a `[...source]` table is not a composer, but they are exercised only as far as these 50 cases reach them -- one valid https URL, one relative and two absolute local paths, and the identifier and ref shapes as used rather than as specified.
inherited_limitations.why: The digest pilot's precedent, and the same reasoning: it ported the SHAPE of `CloneSource` and left `parse_clone_source` to the belt that owns its 57 cases, rather than putting unledgered coverage claims into the tree. The Python implementations stay green in CI throughout, so the rules are not unguarded meanwhile. Approved by the 窓口 with the belt's scope.

inherited_limitations.behaviour: `urlsplit`'s `_check_bracketed_host` defers to `ipaddress.ip_address` in CPython and to `node:net`'s `isIP` here. The two agree on ordinary addresses and may disagree at the edges -- a scoped or otherwise unusual literal.
inherited_limitations.why: No case in this belt's three source files uses a bracketed host. The URL surface is `tests/test_clone_source.py`'s subject and that belt owns closing this. Recorded rather than left for someone to find; `src/domain/python-urlsplit.ts` says the same thing at the line it applies to.

inherited_limitations.behaviour: `expanduser` resolves `~` and NOT `~user`: CPython consults the password database, and where the user is unknown it returns the path unchanged, which is the branch this port always takes.
inherited_limitations.why: Node has no password database. Guessing would put a wrong ABSOLUTE path into a persisted digest, which is worse than the documented gap. A bare `~` -- the spelling `config/projects.local.toml.example` actually documents -- is exact, and no case in these three files uses `~user`.

inherited_limitations.behaviour: Where several keys of one table are invalid, WHICH one is reported first can differ. Python's `dict` iterates in insertion order; JavaScript reorders integer-like keys ahead of the rest, so a table with a key such as `1` (a valid TOML bare key) would be visited in a different order.
inherited_limitations.why: Every key the composer iterates that could be integer-like is a project_id, which `parseIdentifier` refuses anyway -- so the refusal happens either way and only its ORDER could differ, and only for a catalog that is already invalid. Recorded because it is a real difference in behaviour, not because it is reachable by a valid catalog.

entries.target_id: test/application/compose.test.ts::section 5.2: schema version > a non-integer schema_version is refused[1]
entries.reason: The string `"1"`. Refused for not being a number at all, in both languages.

NOT TRANSLATABLE, and it exposes a divergence rather than merely resisting translation. The source passes the Python FLOAT `1.0`: a value equal to `1` and of the wrong type, which `isinstance(version, int)` refuses. JavaScript has a single numeric type in which `1.0 === 1`, so there is no value that reproduces the case -- and, worse, `smol-toml` (like every JavaScript TOML parser) parses `schema_version = 1.0` in a real catalog file to the number `1`, which this port then ACCEPTS. Design doc section 5.2 says a non-integer is refused, so under D-0001's oracle order this is a defect in the port and not a finding against the suite. It is not closable at this layer: the int/float distinction is destroyed by the parser before the composer sees the value, and recovering it would mean re-lexing the TOML. Raised for a decision rather than silently transcribed. The property that DOES exist here -- a number with a fractional part is refused -- is asserted by the target-only test named in `target_only_tests`, so the branch is not left uncovered.

entries.target_id: test/application/compose.test.ts::section 5.2: schema version > a boolean schema_version is refused although bool is an int
entries.reason: Same assertion, and the reason it exists differs between the languages. In Python `bool` IS an `int`, so `isinstance(True, int)` is true and the implementation needs an explicit `isinstance(version, bool)` guard ahead of it. In TypeScript `typeof true` is "boolean" and the guard is redundant -- but it is written anyway and this case still pins it, because the check is a claim about which VALUES are accepted, and a later edit that reordered the guards must not start accepting `true`.

entries.target_id: test/application/compose.test.ts::the composed catalog is not a mutable view > the composed mappings cannot be mutated by a caller
entries.reason: Same assertion and the same exception type. Adapted because `MappingProxyType` has no counterpart: the composer returns FROZEN PLAIN OBJECTS, and an assignment to a frozen object's property throws `TypeError` in a module (always strict mode), which is exactly what the source observes. A `Map` was the other candidate and would have lost the guarantee -- `Object.freeze` does not stop `map.set` -- leaving the claim to the type checker alone.
